fr.recommendations:
• Mark the detached building with a visible address or unit identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main building on arrival.

• Post a site map at the primary access point showing the location of both structures, the internal drive aisle, and any dead-end areas.

• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach both structures.

• Mark the single access point with reflective signage visible from the street in both directions.

• Identify and mark any secondary or emergency-only access point at the rear of the property, even if it requires a gate or barrier to be opened.

• Trim dense vegetation along the drive aisle and walkways to maintain clear sightlines between the access point and both structures.

• Keep walkways between the main building and the detached building clear to allow responder movement on foot between structures.

• Identify a staging area near the access point large enough for multiple emergency vehicles, and keep it free of parked vehicles and landscape materials.

• Mark the parking areas with clear lane boundaries so emergency vehicles can navigate around parked vehicles without confusion.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang close to the building to reduce direct contact between trees and the structure.
• Thin or remove shrubs that are growing immediately against the building walls.
• Keep the landscaped island vegetation trimmed low and free of dead plant material to limit the concentration of burnable material near the building.
• Clear any dead leaves, branches, or debris that collect against the building foundation or along the base of walls.
• Keep the rear of the building accessible by removing any vegetation or stored materials that block movement in that area.
• Maintain the existing open paved areas free of vegetation encroachment along edges and expansion joints.
